role: senior strategy consultant creating the Nexus Home CXO context cockpit
objective: Combine tenant-loaded context with industry movement to explain how the business should run differently, what AI/change bets matter most, and what evidence gates must clear before scale.
ranking_rule: Do not rank by row order. Rank by strategic value, industry urgency, client fit, data/system readiness, risk/control maturity, sponsorship evidence, and dependency leverage.
style: Boardroom-ready strategy language. No product jargon, no raw IDs, no generic AI hype, no unsupported realized value claims.

narrative_sections.enterprise_brief_summary: FS Demo now has an approved Home design pack sourced from active tenant CSVs. The cockpit should tell a CXO what context is loaded, why it matters for AI success, which evidence is missing, and where Intelligence, Moves, Source, and Tower should take over.
narrative_sections.context_confidence_summary: Context confidence separates loaded data from board-grade truth. Stronger answers require source-owner validation, relationship materialization, and evidence lineage.
narrative_sections.evidence_gaps_summary: Evidence gaps are framed as business blockers: what cannot be claimed yet, what source evidence is needed, and which module should own the next action.
narrative_sections.use_cases_summary: AI opportunities are planning-grade until the required systems, data, controls, owners, and value evidence are confirmed.
narrative_sections.proof_summary: The proof tab shows source files, row counts, dates, owners when supplied, fields loaded, and the evidence boundary behind the cockpit.

proof_relationship_visual.title: Context becomes a relationship graph
proof_relationship_visual.caption: Active source rows are converted into a planning-grade graph so aVa can reason across functions, systems, data, vendors, programs, processes, and risks.

dimensions.name: Enterprise Profile
dimensions.summary: A regulated regional bank with fragmented core, digital, risk, and data estate requiring evidence before AI activation.

dimensions.name: Business Functions
dimensions.summary: Lending, fraud, AML/KYC, payments, and wealth operate as distinct functions with limited cross-domain data sharing.

dimensions.name: Org Ownership
dimensions.summary: Data product ownership, control attestation, and AI model accountability are not yet assigned across key domains.

dimensions.name: Workforce Roles
dimensions.summary: Fraud analyst, AML investigator, loan officer, and contact center roles are target beneficiaries; readiness is not evidenced.

dimensions.name: Applications & Systems
dimensions.summary: Core banking, digital, fraud, AML, loan, CRM, and risk platforms operate with incomplete integration and lineage evidence.

dimensions.name: Data Assets & Integrations
dimensions.summary: Data product ownership, control attestation, and AI model accountability are not yet assigned across key domains.

dimensions.name: Infrastructure & Platforms
dimensions.summary: Cloud lakehouse and customer 360 foundation are aspirational; current infrastructure evidence is not yet validated.

dimensions.name: Vendors & Contracts
dimensions.summary: CoreBank, FraudShield, ComplyCase, and others carry unlinked SLA obligations, invoice variances, and exit-right gaps.

dimensions.name: IT Budget, Spend & Value
dimensions.summary: FS Demo operates across lending, cards, payments, fraud, AML/KYC, and wealth under strong regulatory oversight.

dimensions.name: Programs & Initiatives
dimensions.summary: Fraud copilot, AML assist, banker assist, regulatory reporting, customer 360, loan automation, and vendor optimization are active hypotheses.

dimensions.name: AI & Automation Use Cases
dimensions.summary: Lending, fraud, AML/KYC, payments, and wealth operate as distinct functions with limited cross-domain data sharing.

dimensions.name: Risks & Controls
dimensions.summary: Regulatory reporting controls, AML reviewer controls, and fair-lending controls lack linkage to certified data products.

dimensions.name: Relationships
dimensions.summary: CIO, CTO, CDAO, and CRO signals indicate decision latency, contract friction, and sequencing risk across initiatives.

dimensions.name: Evidence Sources
dimensions.summary: No finance-approved baselines, realized savings, or ROI evidence exists for any current AI or modernization initiative.

dimensions.name: Metrics & Outcomes
dimensions.summary: False-positive rates, AML case cycle times, handle times, and defect baselines are absent or not finance-approved.

dimensions.name: Industry Context Patterns
dimensions.summary: Regulated banking AI adoption patterns consistently require lineage, model-risk, and explainability before production deployment.

dimensions.name: Expert Lenses
dimensions.summary: Model risk, AML compliance, fair lending, and data governance expert lenses each surface distinct but compounding blockers.

dimensions.name: Managed Services Scope
dimensions.summary: RegOps Managed Services is identified as a vendor; scope, SLA linkage, and accountability boundaries are not confirmed.

dimensions.name: Operational Process Evidence
dimensions.summary: Lending, fraud, AML/KYC, payments, and wealth operate as distinct functions with limited cross-domain data sharing.
